findings.title: Light/dark values swapped for embedded-post author link
findings.body: This was originally scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The conversion changes the light-theme argument to 70% and uses 30% for the dark-theme $secondary argument, instead of preserving 30% for light and using 70% (100-30) for dark as done elsewhere. Light themes therefore get a much lighter author-link color than before and dark themes get the too-dark value, reversing the intended contrast.

findings.title: Light/dark values swapped for .custom-message-length
findings.body: This was originally scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%). The conversion uses 30% for the light-theme $primary argument and 70% for the dark-theme $secondary argument, instead of preserving 70% for light and using 30% (100-70) for dark. The desktop equivalent at desktop/modal.scss correctly uses 70%/30%; here light themes become substantially darker and dark themes too light.

findings.title: Topic-map h3 light value changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: This was originally scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%). The conversion changes it to dark-light-choose with 50% for light and 50% for dark, instead of preserving 20% for light and using 80% (100-20) for dark. This regresses the light-theme heading color and gives the dark theme insufficient lightness; the desktop equivalent correctly uses 20%/80%.

findings.title: Group-member name light value changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: This .group-member-info .name rule was originally scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The conversion changes it to 50% for light and 50% for dark, instead of preserving 30% for light and using 70% (100-30) for dark. Light-theme rendering therefore changes unintentionally and dark-theme contrast does not follow the pattern used for the identical 30% rules elsewhere.

findings.title: Group-member name light value changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: This .group-member-info .name rule was originally scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The conversion changes it to 50% for light and 50% for dark, instead of preserving 30% for light and using 70% (100-30) for dark. Light-theme rendering therefore changes unintentionally and dark-theme contrast does not follow the pattern used for the identical 30% rules elsewhere.

findings.title: Missed scale-color($primary) conversion in category badge-notification
findings.body: .topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification still uses bare color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%) while every other $primary scale-color in this file was wrapped in dark-light-choose(..., scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)). On a dark theme this remains a darkened/lightened $primary color rather than the intended $secondary-based color, leaving this badge inconsistent and potentially low-contrast.
